Subject: POC plan & risk tracker - Finovate Bank

Thanks for taking the time today, Alex — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment going into the POC:

1) Success criteria (what Finovate will use to evaluate):
   - 95% accuracy on intent classification on your sample set (benchmarked against your current in-house model)
   - End-to-end 95th percentile latency <= 350ms for user-facing flows (50–300 token responses)
   - No customer data exfiltration issues; logging and redaction meet your compliance checklist

2) Evaluation plan / scope:
   - Week 0: access & infra (SSO, API keys, sample dataset)
   - Week 1: model onboarding + baseline tests (we provide scripts)
   - Week 2: integration + end-to-end runs with realistic traffic (10–50 concurrent sessions)
   - Week 3: quality/regression checks and handoff summary

3) Timelines / ownership:
   - Finovate owners: Alex Johnson (product) + Priya Singh (security) — please confirm
   - Redwood owners: Marissa Cole (AM) + Dev Patel (eng lead)

4) Known risks / blockers (initial):
   - Need SSO + service account for sandbox by Wed (3/4) to start week 0
   - Sample dataset format: JSONL with user_id redacted; please include a small representative sample by EOD Tue (3/3)

5) Next steps / actions:
   - Alex: share sample dataset and confirm Priya is included on the thread
   - Dev: prepare onboarding checklist and estimate hours for integration
   - Marissa: share a POC success criteria sheet and risk tracker

Attaching a working template for success criteria and a one-page risk tracker — I will iterate as we get more detail.

[Attachment: POC-success-criteria.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Marissa / team — notes from the eng side after reviewing the sample data format and the success criteria:

1) Items we need from Finovate (blocking until provided):
   - Service account with API key + IP allowlist for sandbox (required to start onboarding)
   - Redacted sample dataset (schema confirmed) + expected QPS pattern (peak concurrent sessions)

2) Technical risks (initial):
   - Large context sessions (>4k tokens) increase memory pressure and can push latency >350ms — mitigation: we will run a trimmed context test and provide recommendations on prefix caching and truncation policies.
   - Quantized model variant: compatibility with certain tokenizer edge cases (we saw tokenization mismatch on named-entity heavy examples). Mitigation: run edge-case tokenization pass and drop-in fix or choose alternative variant.
   - Data retention / logs: need confirmation of log retention window and whether redaction is required before logs are stored.

3) Proposed mitigations & owners:
   - Dev: run tokenization & long-context latency tests by Thu (3/5) and report findings (POC-risk-log.csv attached)
   - Vivek: prepare fallback plan (lower-precision variant + in-memory caching) if latency thresholds fail under load
   - Marissa: coordinate with Alex/Priya on SOC2 artifacts and retention policy requirements

[Attachment: POC-risk-log.csv (CSV)]

Will follow up with a short checklist for SSO setup.

- Dev
